title: Route-level SLI schema and adaptive regional failover with staged load-shedding
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Define a minimal, auditable SLI/SLO declaration format at route (API path) granularity that works per-model and per-variant, specify automated error-budget enforcement semantics, and codify an adaptive regional failover + staged load-shedding policy that integrates with circuit breakers and the Router.

Scope:
- SLI definitions for availability (success-rate), latency (p50/p95/p99 tail), and correctness-class (model response validation pass-rate) at the route+model variant level.
- Error budget accounting model: hourly rolling windows with weighted allocation across route tiers and regional pools, plus explicit borrowing policy for short bursts.
- Enforcement actions mapped to budget states: soft-throttle, prioritized queueing, model-variant fallback, regional reroute, and finally reject-with-graceful-degradation.
- Circuit breaker thresholds tied to quantiles and resource signals (GPU queue depth, scheduler congestion).
- Staged load-shedding algorithm: priority-based eviction > degrade model quality (quantized variant) > route-level reject.
- Observability and runbook ties: dashboards, alert thresholds, incident playbooks, and a small e2e canary test harness.

Decisions and rationale:
1) Route granularity: We chose route-level SLI because different customers and use-cases on the same endpoint exhibit distinct latency and correctness patterns; this enables targeted budgets and safer rollouts for model changes.
2) Rolling hourly windows: Gives fast feedback during traffic spikes while smoothing per-second noise; paired with a 24h aggregated view for trend and burn-rate alerts.
3) Weighted budgets & borrowing: Assign weights by route tier (critical/internal/high-volume/experimental). Borrowing allowed up to 15% of adjacent regional pool budgets for up to 10 minutes to handle failovers. Borrowing is reversible and auditable.
4) Enforcement ladder: Prefer degradations that maintain availability (fallback variants, cached responses) before rejects to minimize customer-visible failures.
5) Circuit breaker inputs: Combine SLI violations (error rate, latency) with infra signals (GPU queue depth > 80%, kernel starvation) to reduce false trips.

Open questions:
- How do we encode correctness-class checks for multimodal outputs (images+text)? Proposal: a small per-route validation suite that produces a pass/fail SLI; initial rollout limited to text routes.
- Exact numeric thresholds for p99 latency and error-rate per route tier — requires analysis of 90 days of historical data (task assigned).

Deliverables:
- SLI/SLO declaration schema (YAML) and validator.
- Implementation of error-budget calculator in the control-plane service.
- Router policy changes: region-aware reroute and staged load-shedding extension.
- Circuit breaker library: configurable thresholds and backoff window.
- Dashboards: per-route burn-rate, borrow-use, and regional capacity heatmaps.
- Runbook: step-by-step mitigation and postmortem checklist.

- Design mockups for console: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1RdS_example_console_designs

- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/router/pull/7890
- Canary harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/slo-canaries/tree/route-level

Acceptance criteria:
- Schema checked into infra repo with unit tests and validator.
- Error-budget service deployed to staging and producing per-route metrics for at least 72h.
- Router honors staged load-shedding policy in canary deployment and fallbacks verified end-to-end.
- Dashboards and alerts exist and on-call runbook updated.
comments: 2026-02-22: Kickoff meeting with PM and Design. Agreed to prioritize text-chat routes in phase 1. Action: Marcus to pull 90-day latency and error history for the top 25 routes.

2026-02-26: Data ingest complete. Early signal: two internal high-volume routes have p99 spikes correlated with KV-cache misses. Added KV cache miss as a signal to consider in circuit-breaker heuristics.

2026-03-01: Architecture review with Runtime and Router teams. Runtime requested a smaller backoff granularity (30s) for circuit-breaker reopen checks to reduce impact on bursty workloads—agreed as opt-in flag.
2026-03-04: Design review: Console needs to show borrow history and per-region budget overlays. Design provided wireframes (Drive link above).
2026-03-06: Prototype PR opened for the error-budget calculator: https://github.com/redwood-inference/control-plane/pull/502. Unit tests added but integration tests pending.
2026-03-08: Post-incident note (INC-2026-11): A regional outage triggered immediate global reroutes; learnings added to policy: cap borrow to 15% and add cooldown of 5 minutes between borrow events.
2026-03-10: Internal demo to SRE and Platform—feedback: add an explicit audit event for route-level enforcement actions for compliance and troubleshooting. Added to TODOs.
Next steps: Finish validator and unit tests (Marcus). Add integration test to canary harness (Aisha). Schedule a cross-team rollout review by 2026-03-18 (owner: PM Sofia Morales).
